extracted.intended_audience: researchers in cognitive neuroscience and psychology studying humor, aggression, or fMRI experimental design
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and analyzing an event-related fMRI experiment that compares point-to-self aggressive vs non-aggressive verbal humor (and their non-humorous counterparts), including stimulus creation, behavioral ratings, personality moderators (self-control, self-construal), image acquisition, preprocessing, and statistical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model of Humor Style (four types)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Martin et al. (2003), categorize verbal humor by direction and interpersonal aggression into: point-to-self non-aggressive humor; point-to-self aggressive humor; point-to-others non-aggressive humor; point-to-others aggressive humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the two dimensions (direction and aggression) to classify stimuli; the paper uses this model as the standard for constructing/labeling materials and for theoretical framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of verbal humor containing social context
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal humor stimuli are defined as 'verbal humor containing social context' (Chan et al., 2012): each humorous story consists of two components — a setup and a punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent setup across experimental and control conditions to isolate humor/comprehension effects; use setup+punchline structure when creating stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive vs non-aggressive criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggressive stories: 'the literal meaning of the punchline in dialogue was derogatory to others'; Non-aggressive stories: 'the literal meaning of the punchline in dialogue was not derogatory to others.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label a stimulus aggressive only if the punchline's literal content is derogatory; produce matched non-aggressive versions by altering punchlines while keeping context; avoid ambiguous boundaries between aggressive and non-aggressive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-to-self definition (direction of humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point-to-self materials are those where the initiator of humor/aggression is another person and the receiver is 'you' (the reader); the last sentence is pointed to the self (people who read stories). This operationalization differs from Martin et al.'s original receiver-based definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid ToM confounds, the study selected point-to-self stories; ensure the final sentence directly addresses the reader to operationalize point-to-self.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus content restrictions and modification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Collected stories must be without sexual content or social taboo; used fictitious names or job titles to replace real names; added reasonable scenes when social context was unclear; simplified story length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control for offensive/taboo content and personal identifiers; standardize length and context; when creating non-humorous counterparts, rewrite the punchline to remove humor while preserving context where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus set size and balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Final stimulus set: 100 materials, four conditions with 25 materials each (AH, AnH, nAH, nAnH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for equal numbers of items per condition to support within-subject contrasts and balanced trial counts across runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability for stimulus classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-rater reliability reported for the four types of materials: 0.951, 0.947, 0.850, and 0.838.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple raters and report inter-rater reliability; strive for high agreement (the study's values indicate very good agreement for some categories and acceptable for others); filter out stimuli with unclear category boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design: 2x2 within-subjects factorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental design is a 2 (aggressive vs non-aggressive) × 2 (humorous vs non-humorous) within-group design; interaction AH–AnH vs nAH–nAnH is of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use within-subject manipulations of both aggression and humor to maximize sensitivity to interaction effects; define interaction contrast explicitly (paper uses (1, -1, -1, 1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial timing and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each trial: jittered fixation (ISI randomly 4, 7, or 10 s), setup shown (participant may press button to proceed but max reading time controlled), punchline presented for 8 s, then two sequential rating questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control reading time by words/reading rate formula; use jittered ISI to decorrelate events; keep punchline presentation constant (8 s) to capture hemodynamic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading time control rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum reading time for the setup = number_of_words / 6 s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure participants have sufficient time to read while keeping timing predictable; check in interviews that participants completed reading before automatic progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-scanner rating procedure and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: During scanning participants answered 'do you feel it funny?' and 'do you feel angry?' with two-point choices (funny/not funny, angry/not angry). Scoring: choice 'funny' or 'angry' = 4 points; 'not' = 0 points; missed (timeout) recorded as 2 points; sum across 25 trials per condition yields 0–100 range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary in-scan ratings minimize motor/time demand; define a scoring rule for missed responses to avoid data loss; aggregate across trials per condition for analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-rating procedure (post-scan)
rubrics_metrics.description: One week after the fMRI experiment, participants re-rated similar materials on a nine-point scale; scores adjusted linearly to 0–100 for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a longer, more granular scale in re-rating to obtain stable evaluations; separate sessions reduce in-scan time pressure effects and allow more detailed subjective ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion and sampling criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants: undergraduate students, native Chinese speakers, right-handed, normal or corrected vision, no reading disorder, ages 18–25; two participants excluded for non-completion leaving N=25. Written informed consent obtained; study approved by ethics committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for handedness and language to reduce variability in lateralization and comprehension; obtain ethics approval and informed consent per Declaration of Helsinki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality moderator measures (self-control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief Self-Control Scale (Tangney et al., 2004), 13 items, Chinese version used; 1–7 Likert; higher scores = higher self-control. Internal consistency in this study: 0.701.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated scales in local language; report Cronbach's alpha; consider sample size implications for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality moderator measures (self-construal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-Construal Scale (Singelis, 1994), 24 items, Chinese version used; independent and interdependent subscales (12 items each), 1–7 Likert; intercultural tendency obtained by subtracting interdependent score from independent score. Internal consistency here: 0.569.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with low internal consistency; if reliability is low, interpret group splits cautiously and consider larger samples or continuous analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping strategy for individual differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants were split into high vs low groups using median or cutoff values (e.g., self-control median 49: high >=50 n=10; low <50 n=15; self-construal median 2: interdependent >=2 n=13; independent <2 n=12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Median-split/grouping is used here due to small sample but authors note limitations; recommended to use continuous scores and larger samples in future studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Scanner and sequences: 3T SIEMENS Prisma, 64-channel head coil. Structural MPRAGE: 0.5 × 0.5 × 1.0 mm in-plane resolution, TR=2530 ms, TI=1100 ms, TE=2.98 ms, flip angle=7°, thickness=1 mm. Functional GE-EPI: 64×64 matrix, TR=2000 ms, TE=30 ms, FOV=224 mm, flip angle=90°, voxel 3.5×3.5×3.5 mm, 33 axial slices thickness 3.5 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report full acquisition parameters to allow replication and interpretation of spatial/temporal resolution; use adequate spatial coverage for regions of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI preprocessing and motion thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprocessing in SPM8: correct for slice timing and head motion, normalize to template, smooth with a 3D Gaussian to improve SNR. Head movement checked: displacement ≤ 1.5 mm and rotation ≤ 1.5° for every participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear motion exclusion criteria and report them; smoothing improves SNR but choose kernel consistent with voxel size and ROI analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-level GLM specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized event-related design model: punchlines modeled as the four experiment conditions (8 s each); six motion parameters entered as covariates; dummy variable encoded scan runs; events convolved with canonical HRF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model the critical event (punchline) explicitly; include motion regressors and run-specific dummy variables to account for session effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast definitions and interaction model
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrasts: humorous minus non-humorous and aggressive minus non-aggressive; interaction defined with (1, -1, -1, 1) to compare AH–AnH vs nAH–nAnH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define contrasts that isolate main effects and interactions of interest; explicitly state contrast vectors for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-level statistical thresholds and cluster definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Group (random effects) analysis: one-sample t-tests voxel-wise with an uncorrected threshold p < 0.001; activated brain regions defined as clusters of more than 10 contiguous voxels at uncorrected p < 0.001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report voxel-wise thresholds and cluster extent criteria; note that uncorrected thresholds and small cluster sizes may inflate false positives — report and justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROI definition and analysis parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: ROIs centered at peaks from main/interaction effects with uncorrected p < 0.001; ROI defined as a 6 mm radius sphere (per Feng et al., 2014). Beta values extracted from ROIs for ANOVA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ROI centers based on independent contrasts or prior literature; specify sphere radius and extraction method; combine ROI analyses with whole-brain results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis methods for behavioral and neural data
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral and neural data analyzed with repeated-measures ANOVA and mixed ANOVA (between-group factors: self-control, self-construal; within-group: humor, aggression). Report F, p, η^2 (effect size), and power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate within- and between-subject models; report effect sizes and power; test interactions and follow-up simple main effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral scoring aggregation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For each participant sum rating scores across 25 trials per condition to produce condition-level scores in the 0–100 range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate trial-level scores into condition-level indices for group comparisons; ensure scoring rules are consistent across in-scan and re-rating sessions (adjust scales to common 0–100 when needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Theory of Mind (ToM) confound
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected point-to-self humor stories because Feng et al. (2014) found point-to-others humor induced more ToM processing; choosing point-to-self helps avoid ToM-related activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the research question targets self-directed humor/emotion, select stimuli that minimize ToM demands; explicitly justify stimulus direction choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, consent, and data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Study approved by institutional Committee for Protecting Human and Animal Subjects; all subjects gave written informed consent in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. Raw data will be made available by the authors upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain institutional ethics approval and informed consent; state data availability for replication and secondary analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors note limitations: small sample size; median-split grouping may induce unstable characterization; self-construal scale reliability was low. They recommend larger samples and using self-control and self-construal as continuous variables in future studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies with adequate sample sizes to support individual-differences analyses; prefer continuous-variable analyses over median splits; check and improve scale reliability in the study population.
